description: Collapse the three full test-suite executions inside one `bun run check:all` into a single captured `bun test --coverage` run that feeds the coverage and skip-ratchet gates in-process.

officialDocsConsulted.version: current (docs served for Bun 1.3.x; local runtime is Bun 1.3.13)
officialDocsConsulted.summary: Confirms the exact seam this PRD depends on: `Bun.spawnSync` returns a `SyncSubprocess` whose `stdout`/`stderr` are `Buffer | undefined` (not `ReadableStream`) and which carries `success` plus `exitCode`; per-stream options are `stdin`/`stdout`/`stderr` with values 'pipe' | 'inherit' | 'ignore'; 'pipe' is the default for stdout and 'inherit' the default for stderr, so BOTH streams must be set to 'pipe' explicitly to capture the suite blob. `maxBuffer` (spawnSync-only) caps captured bytes and kills the child when exceeded, so it must be left unset for a multi-hundred-KB coverage+summary blob. No deprecation or breaking change affecting this change.
officialDocsConsulted.localConventionConflict: This repo's gate spine spawns every gate with stdio fully inherited (`scripts/check-all.ts:131`, and the 'inherit','inherit' generics baked into `SpawnFn` at check-all.ts:34) precisely to keep the operator's live progress visible, while the official capture path requires 'pipe'; RESOLVED FOR THIS PRD in favour of the official pipe form for the suite gate only, with live progress restored by echoing the captured buffers back out after the spawn returns (see US-001 notes: no `tee`/shell form, because every downstream oracle in US-002 and US-003 injects the shared blob through the fake spawn's stdout/stderr Buffers).

MECHANISM IS PINNED, NOT AN OPEN CHOICE: the shared blob MUST derive from the spawn result's piped Buffers (`stdout: 'pipe', stderr: 'pipe'` on the suite spawn only; decode stdout then stderr and concatenate, exactly as the two existing adapters already do at check-coverage.ts:132 and check-skip-ratchet.ts:269), with live progress restored by echoing the captured buffers back to process.stdout/process.stderr after the spawn returns. That means SpawnFn's baked-in 'inherit','inherit' generics (check-all.ts:34) must widen (e.g. to a structural `{ success, exitCode, stdout?: Buffer, stderr?: Buffer }` subset, or `SyncSubprocess<'pipe'|'inherit','pipe'|'inherit'>`); `import type { SyncSubprocess } from 'bun'` stays.

patterns.md bullets to re-read before coding (grep them, do not read the file whole): 'Oracle-friendly manifest design (US-001, CAM-59)' -- keep GATES entries as full space-separated command strings so `g(name, cmdStr)` still splits them and grep-based oracles still match; 'Migrating an injectable SpawnFn seam ... to Bun.spawnSync (US-001, CAM-308)' -- the pass/fail verdict must stay `result.success && result.exitCode === 0` (a signal-killed child reports exitCode null at runtime), and any hand-built SyncSubprocess fixture needs a fully zeroed ResourceUsage object, not a partial cast; 'Oracle-falsifiability rule (US-001, CAM-372)' at patterns.md:928 -- every assertion you add must be swept red against main first.

Bun docs (fetched this plan, see officialDocsConsulted): stdout defaults to 'pipe' but stderr defaults to 'inherit', so BOTH must be set explicitly; leave `maxBuffer` unset (it kills the child once exceeded, and the coverage table plus summary is hundreds of KB).

CAM-474 bracket rule: the oracles above are deliberately bracket-free. If you re-run them, treat exit 2 or a syntax error as an EXTRACTION failure, never as a red criterion.

RAN_LINE_RE already tolerates the singular 'Ran 25 tests across 1 file.' form; do not tighten it.
